cover.title: Mechy Demo bam-v2
cover.subtitle: 4-DOF belt-driven catching arm
notes: Belt-driven 4-DOF arm (base 5.625:1, shoulder 5.625:1, elbow 5.625:1, wrist 4.5:1); every motor sits low, joints turn on 608-2RS / 688-2RS bearings, GT2 closed belts.
Built from design/bam-v2/params.yaml by mechy cad build bam-v2; numbers on these sheets come from the project files named on each sheet.
Estimates are labelled. Read the last sheet (checks, not verified, open decisions) before buying.

reading_notes: Sheets are A4 landscape. Part sheets are true to scale when printed at 100% (scale in the title block); dimensions are in mm.
Third-angle projection: TOP above FRONT, RIGHT beside it. The iso view is not to scale.
Assembly sheets: blue parts are added in that step (moved out a little for clarity).
Every number is computed, from a datasheet, or labelled an estimate; the source file is named on each sheet.

steps.title: Prepare the printed parts
instructions: Print every part in the print list (21 pieces, about 206 g PLA) in the listed orientation.
Clean every bearing bore (F624ZZ / F686ZZ press fits) with a drill bit until a bearing presses in by hand; do not hammer printed seats.
Print the 140 mm shank calibrator too - it sets the homing steps in the last step.

steps.title: Socket and base yaw drive
steps.caption: BLUE = ADDED IN THIS STEP · GREY = ALREADY ASSEMBLED · ARM IN THE READY POSE
instructions: Seat the 51105 thrust bearing in the socket and press the socket into its stand.
Mount the yaw NEMA 17 inside the socket with its 20T pulley (set screw on the flat).
Fit the Z endstop microswitch and wire it to the shield's Z limit header (D11).

steps.title: Main body, motors and belts
steps.caption: BLUE = ADDED IN THIS STEP (MOVED OUT FOR CLARITY) · GREY = ALREADY ASSEMBLED · ARM IN THE READY POSE
instructions: Loop the base GT2 belt over the rotategear and lower the main body onto the 51105.
Mount the two arm NEMA 17s on the main body (Y = lower shank, X = upper/lever), 20T pulleys on both, belts looped but not tensioned.
Bolt on the endstop bracket and stabilizer; fit the Y and X endstop switches.

steps.title: Linkage: shanks, lever, pleuel and levelling links
steps.caption: BLUE = ADDED IN THIS STEP (MOVED OUT FOR CLARITY) · GREY = ALREADY ASSEMBLED · ARM IN THE READY POSE
instructions: Shoulder S: lower shank + lower 90T gear + lever + upper 90T gear share the S axis (F624ZZ bearings). Free rotation, no play.
Pleuel: lever end L to the upper shank's drive pin (F624ZZ); it must stay parallel to the lower shank.
Elbow E: lower shank + upper shank + triplate on one axis (F686ZZ).
Lower levelling link: B0 on the main body to the triplate's rear pin; upper levelling link (BAM part) triplate T2 to the manipulator T3.
Wrist W: manipulator on the upper shank end (F686ZZ). The linkage keeps it level.

steps.title: Toolhead
steps.caption: BLUE = ADDED IN THIS STEP (MOVED OUT FOR CLARITY) · GREY = ALREADY ASSEMBLED · ARM IN THE READY POSE
hardware: gripper motor (28BYJ; ref_arm uses a servo)
instructions: Cup: bolt the cup flange to the manipulator plate (M3 into the printed flange; the cup opening points straight up).
Stick the foam liner ring inside the cup wall.

steps.title: Electronics
instructions: Plug the three A4988 drivers into X/Y/Z (EN to EN), set MS1/MS2/MS3 jumpers for the chosen microsteps and Vref BEFORE connecting the belts (wiring sheet).
Motors: X = upper arm, Y = lower arm, Z = yaw. Endstops to the matching limit headers.
100 uF capacitor across the shield's motor power input, 24 V supply, Arduino on USB. Never unplug a motor with the supply on.
Flash the generated firmware (flashing steps on the wiring sheet).

steps.title: Home and calibrate
steps.caption: BLUE = BELTS TO TENSION · ARM IN THE READY POSE
instructions: Mount the shank calibrator and set X_HOME_STEPS / Y_HOME_STEPS / Z_HOME_STEPS per the control README (the generated values are estimates until calibrated).
Home order: shoulder, elbow, base (the wrist is passive - the linkage levels it).
Send HOME with a hand on the power switch; each joint must stop cleanly at its endstop.

tension_notes: base: slide the motor in its slots until the 200.0 mm belt deflects about 2.0 mm under a light finger press mid-span (about 1/64 of the span, a common GT2 rule of thumb; estimate), then tighten.
shoulder: slide the motor in its slots until the 200.0 mm belt deflects about 2.0 mm under a light finger press mid-span (about 1/64 of the span, a common GT2 rule of thumb; estimate), then tighten.
elbow: slide the motor in its slots until the 200.0 mm belt deflects about 2.0 mm under a light finger press mid-span (about 1/64 of the span, a common GT2 rule of thumb; estimate), then tighten.
Link belts (520 mm): stock loops sized exactly to the 220 mm centre distance; take up slack with the slotted shaft holes (+-3 mm) before clamping the collars.
Home in this order: shoulder, elbow, base, wrist. Send HOME with a hand on the power switch and check each joint stops at its sensor (table on the belts and homing sheet).

homing.homes: q0 at the Z endstop; calibrate with Z_HOME_STEPS
a1 = q1 at the Y endstop; recalibrate with tool_shank_calibrator_140
a2 = q1+q2 at the X endstop; recalibrate with the calibrator

homing.sensor: none (passive joint: the linkage holds q3 = -(q1+q2))

motor_notes: belt pass-through: the elbow motor sets the forearm's absolute pitch q1+q2 and the wrist motor the hand's q1+q2+q3; moving the shoulder alone keeps forearm and cup pitch fixed
motor_angle = gear_ratio * (C @ q); steps = round(steps_per_rad * (C @ q)); q = C^-1 @ (motor_angle / gear_ratio); motor torque = (C^-T tau_joint) / gear_ratio
Steps per degree of the motor-side angle at 8 microsteps: base 25, shoulder 25, elbow 25, wrist 20

No new CAD until your pick. All retain four owned motors, wrist roll, MG90S, black finish, X1E fit target and PETG exceptions. Grip, exact motor/step-rate capability and delivered cost below $100 remain unverified; choosing a concept does not approve fabrication or a budget increase.
